<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - F2 is a Python‑based, multi‑platform content downloader and data‑processing library with both a CLI and programmable API interfaces.  
   - It provides out‑of‑the‑box support for Douyin, TikTok, Twitter, WeiBo, Bark, and is designed to be extensible for future platforms.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top‑level “f2” folder: the application code, subdivided into:  
     • apps/…: one subpackage per supported platform, each with api.py, cli.py, crawler.py, dl.py, db.py, filter.py, handler.py, model.py, utils.py  
     • cli/: core command processor and console front‑end  
     • conf/: YAML configuration files and conf‑manager utilities  
     • crawlers/: base_crawler.py defines HTTP & WebSocket request framework  
     • dl/: base_downloader.py for standardized download workflows  
     • db/: base_db.py for storage (sqlite via aiosqlite)  
     • exceptions/: custom error types  
     • i18n/, languages/: localization support  
     • log/: centralized logger  
     • utils/: shared helpers (singleton, signal, JSON filters, abogus/xbogus algorithms)  
   - tests/ and f2/apps/*/test: unit and integration tests  
   - docs/ & .vitepress/: website‑generation for end‑user documentation

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Confirms CLI usage, configuration files (app.yaml, conf.yaml, defaults.yaml), and extensibility points.  
   - Describes features (fetch_user_profile, fetch_one_video, fetch_live_im, etc.), notification integration (Bark), and advanced guides.

4. Designing the system architecture diagram  
   a. Main components  
      - User (CLI or Python API client)  
      - CLI Front‑end (f2/cli) or Programmatic Entry (f2/__main__.py)  
      - Command Processor & Dispatcher  
      - Platform‑Specific Module Loader (f2/apps/*)  
      - Shared Services:  
         • Configuration Manager (f2/conf & f2/utils/conf_manager.py)  
         • Crawler Layer (f2/crawlers/base_crawler.py)  
         • Downloader Layer (f2/dl/base_downloader.py)  
         • Data Storage (f2/db/base_db.py + aiosqlite)  
         • Logging (f2/log/logger.py)  
         • Internationalization (f2/i18n/translator.py + language packs)  
         • Utilities & Algorithms (XBogus, ABogus managers, token/signature generators)  
      - External Services:  
         • Social‑media HTTP APIs (Douyin, TikTok, Twitter, WeiBo)  
         • WebSocket endpoints for live‑stream IM  
         • Notification Service (Bark HTTP API)  
   b. Relationships & interactions  
      - User → CLI/API → Command Processor  
      - Command Processor → Loads platform module → Invokes api/crawler/dl/db/filter in sequence  
      - Crawler → HTTP/WebSocket call → External platform → returns raw data  
      - Filter/Model → transforms raw data → Data Storage (optional) → File System (downloads)  
      - Logging and i18n intercept at each layer  
      - Config Manager supplies credentials, endpoints, feature flags  
   c. Architectural patterns & principles  
      - Plugin‑style “apps” for each platform (extensible, isolated code)  
      - Shared base classes for crawler/downloader/db to enforce consistency  
      - Separation of concerns: CLI vs core logic vs persistence vs networking  
      - Asynchronous I/O for network and file operations (httpx, websockets, aiosqlite)  
      - Dependency injection via config manager  
   d. Relevant technologies/libraries  
      - click or rich for CLI console  
      - httpx for HTTP requests  
      - websockets for live‑streaming  
      - protobuf for live‑cast messages  
      - pydantic for data models  
      - aiosqlite for persistence  
      - PyExecJS & cryptography for signature algorithms  

5. Guidelines for tailoring the diagram  
   - Focus on core‑tool architecture and extensibility: show distinct “apps” submodules as plugin boxes around a central core.  
   - Highlight how CLI/API clients interface with the core, and how the core interacts with External Services.  
   - Use swimlanes or layers: User Layer, Presentation (CLI/API) Layer, Application Core Layer, Infrastructure Layer, External Services Layer.  

6. Diagram‑drawing instructions  
   - Use clear rectangular boxes for each component (e.g., “CLI Front‑end”, “Config Manager”, “BaseCrawler”).  
   - Connect them with directional arrows to show call flow (e.g., CLI → Command Processor → Platform Module → Crawler → External API).  
   - Color‑code by layer:  
      • Presentation (blue)  
      • Core Services (green)  
      • Infrastructure (orange)  
      • External (purple)  
   - Annotate arrows with protocol or data format (e.g., HTTP/JSON, WebSocket/protobuf).  
   - Label plugin points (e.g., f2/apps/douyin, f2/apps/tiktok) to emphasize extensibility.  
   - Add legends for colors and shapes.

By decomposing F2 into these components and layers—CLI/API entry, platform‑specific plugins, shared services (config, crawler, downloader, db, logging, i18n), and external interactions—you will produce a detailed, accurate system design diagram that captures both the breadth (multiple platforms) and depth (core services) of the project.  
</explanation>
